subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal first, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat/Discord retry parity before treating the transient-drop bug as fixed?
rationale: Current source shows both a shared root conflict throw and surface-level terminalization paths, while the latest comment argues that the proof-positive shared PR may fix a permanent wedge but not the transient retry-parity problem.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest the reported WebChat, heartbeat, and Discord transient paths before adding channel-specific loops.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and require explicit retry/requeue or visible-failure handling for the remaining non-Telegram surfaces before this issue can close.

options.title: Ask For One More Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a current-main WebChat or heartbeat timing repro focused on distinct messageIds before choosing between shared recovery and surface retry parity.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest the reported WebChat, heartbeat, and Discord transient paths before adding channel-specific loops.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest current-main history on the guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where this owner-boundary decision sits.
